- Market leadership in the datasets that matter most - private-company financials in India described as best-in-class, wider than any other platform in India or globally
- Vertical-teams playbook set up in FY24 - each key customer segment run as a mini business unit with its own sales pitch, channels, engagement model and offering priorities; management says it continues to deliver and that sales conversions have improved

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Storage of data, security and fraud — Named explicitly as key risk categories in the Company's Risk Management Policy. For a business whose entire product is a proprietary database covering millions of private companies, data storage and security sit at the centre of the asset itself; the Corporate Governance Report separately notes the Company 'has in place relevant information security policies that ensure proper utilisation of IT resources'.
- Reputation and market risk — Named as a key risk category in the Risk Management Policy. The AR positions Tracxn as the cited 'reference source' for private markets in media and research, so reputational damage would erode the distribution and credibility the platform's positioning rests on.
- Strategic risk, including how AI reshapes the private-markets data layer — 'Strategic' is a named category in the Risk Management Policy. The Chairman/MD letter states that 'the question of how AI changes the data layer sat at the centre of every customer conversation' during the year - management's stated view is that AI is a tailwind and 'accretive to our long-term thesis, not a challenge against it', but the disclosure itself confirms this is the central strategic uncertainty customers are raising. [AI framing back-filled from the Chairman/MD letter, routed into the profile and strategy_outlook sibling bundles.]
- Human resource and key-person risk — 'Human Resource' is a named category in the Risk Management Policy. The Company had 717 employees as at the end of FY 2025-26 including the executive directors, and is an entirely people-and-data business with no physical assets; the two founders are also the two Executive Directors, and the growth plan depends on scaling closing-sales teams in India and internationally. The Board's Report also records churn in a statutory role during the year (the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer changed on June 02, 2025).
- Legal, compliance and taxation risk - including the new Labour Codes — 'Legal and Compliance' and 'Taxation and Financial' are named categories in the Risk Management Policy. Separately, the Corporate Overview's own footnote identifies an FY26 exceptional item as a 'Provision towards impact due to new Labour Codes', i.e. a regulatory change has already crystallised into a charge for an employee-cost-heavy business. [Labour Codes reference back-filled from the capex_expansion sibling bundle; the amount is a P&L figure and is deliberately not reproduced.]
- Economic and operational risk — Named as a key risk category in the Risk Management Policy. The customer base is concentrated in private-market participants - venture capital and private equity funds, investment banks and corporate development teams - whose own activity levels are cyclical with the funding environment.
- Structural concentration: one entity, one segment, one platform, with operations in a single country serving a majority-international revenue base — The Company has no subsidiaries or associate companies and prepares standalone accounts for one entity; the Board reviews operations as one single segment with no separate reportable segments. Nearly 55% of revenue is generated internationally from customers across more than 50 countries while the entire operations are based out of India - management presents this 'Make in India, Sell Globally' structure as a cost advantage, but it is simultaneously a currency, cross-border and single-location operating concentration. [Back-filled from the Board's Report and Corporate Overview, routed into the profile, capex_expansion and strategy_outlook sibling bundles - no concentration disclosure of any kind reached the risks bundle.]
- No Risk Management Committee at Board level (stated non-applicability) — A stated absence, and a real finding: 'Risk Management Committee as required under Regulation 21 of SEBI Listing Regulations and applicable to top 1000 companies, is not applicable for your Company.' Risk oversight therefore rests on a Board-adopted Risk Management Policy and the Audit Committee rather than on a dedicated committee. The Board has constituted only three committees (Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders' Relationship), and the Corporate Social Responsibility Committee was dissolved with effect from May 25, 2026.

business.body: Tracxn is a private market intelligence platform that helps investors and companies discover, monitor and track startups and private companies around the world, supporting deal sourcing, due diligence, market mapping, competitive analysis and funding-trend tracking. outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deepen the position as the global reference platform for private-markets data through sizable platform investments - depth of datasets, breadth of regulatory-data coverage, specialised teams and AI capabilities - made particularly in India in FY26.
- Run the vertical-teams playbook set up in FY24: a specialised mini business unit per key customer segment (investment banking, corporate sales, universities, and other segments), each with its own sales pitch, channels, customer engagement model and offering priorities.
- Replicate the India playbook - vertical teams plus prioritised dataset launches - across international geographies, with dataset launches and sales-team expansions planned through the year.
- Scale sales capacity: double the India closing-sales team from ~25 to ~40 by end CY26 and scale the international closing-sales team from under 10 to ~25.
- Expand datasets primarily for international geographies, with major investments underway in valuation and revenue data (especially in the US) and CXO data across the US and Europe.
- Continue deepening coverage of regulatory data across key geographies.
- Embed AI across the whole business - back end (identify, classify, deduplicate and enrich entities at scale, accelerating data production and structuring), front end (Tracxn Connector for Claude; an AI-chat assistant on the platform in private beta), and internal functions such as support and HR - treated as a way of working rather than a single initiative.
- Open AI-native access as a NEW DISTRIBUTION CHANNEL, letting investors and corporates use Tracxn data inside their own AI-native workflows, including through partnerships with other AI-native platforms.
- Launch coverage of the datasets customers are asking for, including comprehensive global coverage of AI-native companies, in response to rising customer interest.
- Be the reference source cited whenever media writes about private markets, sustained through media partnerships and report tie-ups.
- Grow within existing accounts by selling additional seats, alongside new-customer acquisition.
- Preserve the 'Make in India, Sell Globally' structure - entire operations based out of India serving a global customer base - as a durable cost advantage versus global peers.
- Return capital to shareholders as a stated discipline, evidenced by the first buyback as a listed company executed in H1 FY26.
- Aspiration (stated, non-checkable): become a dominant global player in the private-market data space.
- STATED ABSENCE OF GROUP STRUCTURE: the Company has no subsidiaries or associate companies, so the financial statements are prepared for one entity on a standalone basis, and the Board reviews operations as one single segment with no separate reportable segments [stated in the Board's Report, routed into the profile and capex_expansion sibling bundles]. The stated philosophy is asset-light and self-funded - the business has been debt free since inception, does not require any major capital expenditure, and the free cash it generates is described as available both for investing in growth and for returning to shareholders. On distributions, the Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy pursuant to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, published on its website, setting out the broad principles guiding the Board and management on declaration and distribution of dividend; for FY26, because the Company did not have profits, no amount was transferred to reserves and the Board did not recommend any dividend. On buybacks, the Board on May 26, 2025 approved, and shareholders approved by postal ballot on July 03, 2025 (result declared July 07, 2025), a tender-offer buyback of a maximum size of INR 7,99,99,990 (excluding transaction costs and taxes) at a price not exceeding INR 75 per share, with a Buyback Committee constituted for it; the offer, open to all equity shareholders OTHER THAN the Promoters and the Promoter Group, ran from July 24, 2025 to July 30, 2025, and 10,66,666 equity shares were bought back and extinguished at INR 75 per share, with the certificate of extinguishment filed with SEBI on August 13, 2025. Management describes this - its first buyback as a listed company - as reflecting conviction in the long-term value of the business and a discipline of returning capital to shareholders. The Company neither invited nor accepted any public deposits during the year and had no principal or interest on public deposits outstanding as at March 31, 2026. [Dividend, buyback, deposits and debt-free statements are from the Board's Report and Chairman/MD letter, routed into the profile and strategy_outlook sibling bundles.]
- Risk Management Policy adopted and a mechanism implemented for risk assessment and management, providing for identification of possible business risks, assessment at regular intervals and appropriate measures and controls to manage, mitigate and handle them; the policy's named risk categories are Reputation and Market Risk, Legal and Compliance, Economic and Operational, Storage of data, Security and Fraud, Strategic, Taxation and Financial, and Human Resource. Policy published on the Company's website.
- Whistle Blower Policy adopted with vigil mechanisms for Directors and employees under Section 177(9) of the Act, safeguarding them from victimisation when raising concerns about violations of legal or regulatory requirements or misrepresentation of financial statements; employees may report directly to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee, and all complaints are periodically placed before the Audit Committee. STATED NIL: 'No complaints were received by your Company under the Whistle Blower Policy during FY 2025-26.'
- STATED CHANGE (real finding): the Corporate Social Responsibility Committee was DISSOLVED with effect from May 25, 2026 (the Board's Report points to note no. 32 for details, which was not routed into this bundle).
- Workforce: 717 employees as at the end of FY 2025-26, including the executive directors.
- Diversity: women comprise 42% of the workforce; the Board as on March 31, 2026 included one woman Executive Director (who is also the Chairperson and Managing Director) and one woman Independent Director. [Workforce diversity figure back-filled from the Chairman/MD letter, routed into the profile and strategy_outlook sibling bundles; Board composition from the Board's Report.]
- Employee benefits: a gratuity fund has been formed exclusively for gratuity payment to employees, named the 'Tracxn Employees' Group Gratuity Scheme' (in force with effect from 15th March 2024).
- Governance-of-people policies: a Nomination and Remuneration Policy is in place covering criteria for appointment, removal and retirement of Directors and Managerial Personnel INCLUDING qualification and diversity requirements, remuneration policy for Executive / Non-Executive / Independent Directors and Managerial Personnel, and familiarisation programmes for Directors; a formal annual evaluation of the Board, its Committees and individual Directors is conducted via a rating-scale questionnaire, and the Independent Directors met separately on March 18, 2026 to evaluate the Board as a whole, the Non-Independent Directors and the Chairperson.
- A policy on Related Party Transactions has been adopted (statement truncated mid-sentence in the source, so its content is unavailable).
- NO QUANTIFIED ESG TARGET IS DISCLOSED ANYWHERE IN THE ROUTED TEXT - no BRSR content was supplied at all (no Section A entity details, no material responsible-business-conduct issues table, no energy, emissions, water, waste, safety, POSH, CSR-spend or community data). The ESG list above is therefore governance-and-people disclosure from the Board's Report, not sustainability performance; the absence of any environmental or social metric is itself the finding.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Tracxn has no physical expansion programme and says so plainly: the Board's Report states the business 'is asset-light and has been debt free since inception', the Corporate Overview states it 'is digital, scalable, and doesn't require heavy physical infrastructure', and the Key Business Attributes spread states that 'the business does not require any major capital expenditure'. Expansion is therefore expressed as platform, dataset, distribution and sales-capacity build-out rather than plants, lines or capacity. In FY26 the Company made sizable platform investments, particularly in India, across the depth of its datasets, the breadth of its regulatory-data coverage, the strengthening of specialised teams and the advancement of its AI capabilities; significant new datasets were added without a meaningful increase in headcount, the clearest example being coverage of private-company financials in India, built within a year to what management calls best-in-class and wider than any other platform in India or globally, plus comprehensive global coverage of AI-native companies. Looking forward, major international dataset investments are underway - valuation and revenue data (especially in the US) and CXO data across the US and Europe - with some already launched and several large launches planned through FY27, and coverage of regulatory data is to be deepened further across key geographies. Distribution build-out is the second axis: the India closing-sales team is to double from about 25 to about 40 by the end of CY26 and the international closing-sales team is to scale from under 10 to about 25, on top of the FY24 vertical-team structure in which each key customer segment is run as a mini business unit. The third axis is AI: back-end automation of data production and structuring, and a front-end distribution channel comprising the Tracxn Connector for Claude (live for paid users), an AI-chat assistant on the platform in private beta, and partnerships with other AI-native platforms, expected to start contributing to revenue from FY27. Delivery capacity is organised as customer-success and engagement teams aligned to geographies, customer segments and time zones, with inside-sales shifts covering APAC1 (8am-6pm IST), APAC2 (9am-7pm IST), EMEA (12pm-9pm IST), US East (3pm-12am IST) and US West (6pm-3am IST). [The forward dataset and sales-capacity plans in this paragraph are stated in the Chairman/MD 'Letter to Shareholders', which was routed into the profile and strategy_outlook sibling bundles, not into this one - see extraction notes.]
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Large and largely unpenetrated addressable market: over 300,000 addressable organisations across investment firms, financial institutions, large MNCs, startups, government bodies and academic institutions, with only a small percentage currently served by structured data platforms. [back-filled from the capex_expansion sibling bundle, 'KEY BUSINESS ATTRIBUTES - a. Large and growing market'; no MD&A chapter was routed into this bundle]
- Customer-universe expansion: the number of institutional investors has grown around three times in the last decade, and as the private market evolves more players with newer use cases and requirements arise. [back-filled from the capex_expansion sibling bundle]
- Structural demand tailwind stated in the founding narrative: with more capital flowing into startups and companies staying private for longer, the demand for private market data was only set to rise.
- India is the high-momentum geography, and management says the pace of growth itself stepped up in Q4 FY26; the acceleration is attributed first to the vertical teams and more recently to launching significant additional datasets prioritised by those teams.
- Dataset launches are the stated driver of the India Q4 acceleration (launches executed in Q3 and Q4 FY26), which management expects to continue and accelerate through FY27, compounded by larger sales capacity and improved sales conversions.
- AI is framed as a meaningful tailwind rather than a threat: it deepens the moat at the data layer, opens a new distribution channel at the customer-interface layer, and lets Tracxn go deeper into customer workflows than before; management calls it accretive to the long-term thesis.
- AI-driven automation lets the platform scale efficiently - significant new datasets were added in FY26 without a meaningful increase in headcount.
- Operating leverage as the margin lever: after the initial investment in technology infrastructure, proprietary data assets and workflow automation, the incremental cost of serving additional customers is minimal and the platform is entirely productized with no custom development per customer; management states that when growth accelerates margins improve quickly and expects non-linear EBITDA expansion once growth re-accelerates from the FY26 investments. [the specific historical incremental-revenue-to-EBITDA conversion rate quoted alongside this claim is a P&L-derived figure and has been withheld]
- FY26 margins were explicitly described as impacted by continued investments in growth, i.e. the current year is an investment year rather than a harvest year.
- India cost advantage: nearly 55% of revenue is generated internationally from customers in more than 50 countries while the entire operations are based out of India, which management describes as a significant, sustainable cost advantage and a competitive advantage in profitability and scale-up versus global peers.
- Account-level headroom: besides new customers there is significant depth for expansion within each account by selling additional seats, with the cumulative count of accounts above successive annual-accrued-revenue tiers cited as evidence of ongoing headroom for realised pricing growth. [back-filled from the capex_expansion sibling bundle]
- Segment-level momentum stated qualitatively: investment banking accounts growing in India and internationally with month-on-month market-share gains; corporate sales accounts growing; university accounts growing with Tracxn embedded into coursework. [the accompanying segment revenue-growth percentages are P&L-derived and have been withheld]
- Newly launched AI capabilities (Connector for Claude, platform AI assistant) launched just after FY26 close and therefore do NOT appear in FY26 revenue - a stated timing driver for FY27.
- Cash generation: management states the business model is inherently cash generating like any SaaS business and does not require any major capital expenditure, leaving free cash available for investing in growth as well as returning to shareholders. [back-filled from the capex_expansion sibling bundle; the rupee cash figures are withheld]
